              "// limitations under the License.\n",
              "\n",
              "/**\n",
              " * @fileoverview Helpers for google.colab Python module.\n",
              " */\n",
              "(function(scope) {\n",
              "function span(text, styleAttributes = {}) {\n",
              "  const element = document.createElement('span');\n",
              "  element.textContent = text;\n",
              "  for (const key of Object.keys(styleAttributes)) {\n",
              "    element.style[key] = styleAttributes[key];\n",
              "  }\n",
              "  return element;\n",
              "}\n",
              "\n",
              "// Max number of bytes which will be uploaded at a time.\n",
              "const MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE = 100 * 1024;\n",
              "\n",
              "function _uploadFiles(inputId, outputId) {\n",
              "  const steps = uploadFilesStep(inputId, outputId);\n",
              "  const outputElement = document.getElementById(outputId);\n",
              "  // Cache steps on the outputElement to make it available for the next call\n",
              "  // to uploadFilesContinue from Python.\n",
              "  outputElement.steps = steps;\n",
              "\n",
              "  return _uploadFilesContinue(outputId);\n",
              "}\n",
              "\n",
              "// This is roughly an async generator (not supported in the browser yet),\n",
              "// where there are multiple asynchronous steps and the Python side is going\n",
              "// to poll for completion of each step.\n",
              "// This uses a Promise to block the python side on completion of each step,\n",
              "// then passes the result of the previous step as the input to the next step.\n",
              "function _uploadFilesContinue(outputId) {\n",
              "  const outputElement = document.getElementById(outputId);\n",
              "  const steps = outputElement.steps;\n",
              "\n",
              "  const next = steps.next(outputElement.lastPromiseValue);\n",
              "  return Promise.resolve(next.value.promise).then((value) => {\n",
              "    // Cache the last promise value to make it available to the next\n",
              "    // step of the generator.\n",
              "    outputElement.lastPromiseValue = value;\n",
              "    return next.value.response;\n",
              "  });\n",
              "}\n",
              "\n",
              "/**\n",
              " * Generator function which is called between each async step of the upload\n",
              " * process.\n",
              " * @param {string} inputId Element ID of the input file picker element.\n",
              " * @param {string} outputId Element ID of the output display.\n",
              " * @return {!Iterable<!Object>} Iterable of next steps.\n",
              " */\n",
              "function* uploadFilesStep(inputId, outputId) {\n",
              "  const inputElement = document.getElementById(inputId);\n",
              "  inputElement.disabled = false;\n",
              "\n",
              "  const outputElement = document.getElementById(outputId);\n",
              "  outputElement.innerHTML = '';\n",
              "\n",
              "  const pickedPromise = new Promise((resolve) => {\n",
              "    inputElement.addEventListener('change', (e) => {\n",
              "      resolve(e.target.files);\n",
              "    });\n",
              "  });\n",
              "\n",
              "  const cancel = document.createElement('button');\n",
              "  inputElement.parentElement.appendChild(cancel);\n",
              "  cancel.textContent = 'Cancel upload';\n",
              "  const cancelPromise = new Promise((resolve) => {\n",
              "    cancel.onclick = () => {\n",
              "      resolve(null);\n",
              "    };\n",
              "  });\n",
              "\n",
              "  // Wait for the user to pick the files.\n",
              "  const files = yield {\n",
              "    promise: Promise.race([pickedPromise, cancelPromise]),\n",
              "    response: {\n",
              "      action: 'starting',\n",
              "    }\n",
              "  };\n",
              "\n",
              "  cancel.remove();\n",
              "\n",
              "  // Disable the input element since further picks are not allowed.\n",
              "  inputElement.disabled = true;\n",
              "\n",
              "  if (!files) {\n",
              "    return {\n",
              "      response: {\n",
              "        action: 'complete',\n",
              "      }\n",
              "    };\n",
              "  }\n",
              "\n",
              "  for (const file of files) {\n",
              "    const li = document.createElement('li');\n",
              "    li.append(span(file.name, {fontWeight: 'bold'}));\n",
              "    li.append(span(\n",
              "        `(${file.type || 'n/a'}) - ${file.size} bytes, ` +\n",
              "        `last modified: ${\n",
              "            file.lastModifiedDate ? file.lastModifiedDate.toLocaleDateString() :\n",
              "                                    'n/a'} - `));\n",
              "    const percent = span('0% done');\n",
              "    li.appendChild(percent);\n",
              "\n",
              "    outputElement.appendChild(li);\n",
              "\n",
              "    const fileDataPromise = new Promise((resolve) => {\n",
              "      const reader = new FileReader();\n",
              "      reader.onload = (e) => {\n",
              "        resolve(e.target.result);\n",
              "      };\n",
              "      reader.readAsArrayBuffer(file);\n",
              "    });\n",
              "    // Wait for the data to be ready.\n",
              "    let fileData = yield {\n",
              "      promise: fileDataPromise,\n",
              "      response: {\n",
              "        action: 'continue',\n",
              "      }\n",
              "    };\n",
              "\n",
              "    // Use a chunked sending to avoid message size limits. See b/62115660.\n",
              "    let position = 0;\n",
              "    do {\n",
              "      const length = Math.min(fileData.byteLength - position, MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE);\n",
              "      const chunk = new Uint8Array(fileData, position, length);\n",
              "      position += length;\n",
              "\n",
              "      const base64 = btoa(String.fromCharCode.apply(null, chunk));\n",
              "      yield {\n",
              "        response: {\n",
              "          action: 'append',\n",
              "          file: file.name,\n",
              "          data: base64,\n",
              "        },\n",
              "      };\n",
              "\n",
              "      let percentDone = fileData.byteLength === 0 ?\n",
              "          100 :\n",
              "          Math.round((position / fileData.byteLength) * 100);\n",
              "      percent.textContent = `${percentDone}% done`;\n",
              "\n",
              "    } while (position < fileData.byteLength);\n",
              "  }\n",
              "\n",
              "  // All done.\n",
              "  yield {\n",
              "    response: {\n",
              "      action: 'complete',\n",
              "    }\n",
              "  };\n",
              "}\n",
              "\n",
              "scope.google = scope.google || {};\n",
              "scope.google.colab = scope.google.colab || {};\n",
              "scope.google.colab._files = {\n",
              "  _uploadFiles,\n",
              "  _uploadFilesContinue,\n",
              "};\n",
              "})(self);\n",
              "</script> "
            ]
          },
          "metadata": {}
        },

        "# Import the files module from google.colab to handle file uploads\n",
        "from google.colab import files\n",

        "# Read the uploaded CSV file into a pandas DataFrame\n",
        "df = pd.read_csv(file_name)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Display the first 5 rows of the DataFrame to confirm successful loading\n",
        "display(df.head())"

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "5f840fd1"
      },
      "source": [
        "## Data Dictionary or Descriptions\n",
        "\n",
        "Here's a breakdown of what each column in this dataset represents:\n",
        "\n",
        "*   **PassengerId**: A unique identifier for each passenger.\n",
        "*   **Survived**: Indicates whether the passenger survived the disaster (0 = No, 1 = Yes).\n",
        "*   **Pclass**: The passenger's class (1 = 1st class, 2 = 2nd class, 3 = 3rd class).\n",
        "*   **Name**: The name of the passenger.\n",
        "*   **Sex**: The gender of the passenger (male/female).\n",
        "*   **Age**: The age of the passenger.\n",
        "*   **SibSp**: Number of siblings/spouses aboard the Titanic.\n",
        "*   **Parch**: Number of parents/children aboard the Titanic.\n",
        "*   **Ticket**: The ticket number.\n",
        "*   **Fare**: The fare paid for the ticket.\n",
        "*   **Cabin**: The cabin number.\n",
        "*   **Embarked**: The port where the passenger embarked (C = Cherbourg, Q = Queenstown, S = Southampton)."
      ]
    },

        "id": "43qBv0NdflAK"
      }

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "35394593"
      },
      "source": [
        "### Box Plot for Age\n",
        "\n",
        "This box plot will help visualize the distribution of ages and identify any unusual age values (outliers)."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/",
          "height": 526
        },
        "id": "0bae720d",
        "outputId": "a1f86b2a-1a28-4b8c-97bf-d531ad9f6b9b"
      },
      "source": [
        "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))\n",
        "sns.boxplot(y=df['Age'], ax=ax)\n",
        "ax.set_title('Box Plot of Age')\n",
        "ax.set_ylabel('Age')\n",
        "plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)\n",
        "plt.show()"
      ],
      "execution_count": null,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "display_data",

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "# Step 5: Univariate Analysis"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "tY2UuQl5mQJq"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "Numerical Variable Analysis"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "9--uogrvo8pZ"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/",
          "height": 1000
        },
        "id": "15af9cd1",
        "outputId": "9422bbf0-55cf-4e4b-8ea3-032508ace172"
      },
      "source": [
        "# Define numerical columns that are suitable for distribution analysis\n",
        "# PassenpgerId and Ticket are unique identifiers and will be handled separately\n",
        "numerical_cols = ['Age', 'Fare', 'SibSp', 'Parch']\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Descriptive Statistics for Numerical Columns:\")\n",
        "display(df[numerical_cols].describe())\n",
        "\n",
        "# Loop through each numerical column to create a histogram\n",
        "for col in numerical_cols:\n",
        "    # Create a figure and an axes object for the plot\n",
        "    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))\n",
        "    # Create a histogram with KDE (Kernel Density Estimate) for the current column\n",
        "    # KDE provides a smoothed representation of the distribution\n",
        "    sns.histplot(df[col], kde=True, ax=ax, bins=20) # Use 20 bins for better detail\n",
        "    # Set the title of the plot for clarity\n",
        "    ax.set_title(f'Distribution of {col}')\n",
        "    # Set the label for the x-axis\n",
        "    ax.set_xlabel(col)\n",
        "    # Set the label for the y-axis\n",
        "    ax.set_ylabel('Frequency')\n",
        "    # Add a grid for easier reading of values\n",
        "    plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)\n",
        "    # Display the plot\n",
        "    plt.show()\n",
        "\n",
        "    # Explanation of what the chart helps understand\n",
        "    if col == 'Age':\n",
        "        print(f\"The histogram for '{col}' shows the age distribution of passengers. We can observe the most common age groups and the spread of ages. It helps identify if the data is skewed, bimodal, or has outliers.\")\n",
        "    elif col == 'Fare':\n",
        "        print(f\"The histogram for '{col}' reveals the distribution of ticket prices. It helps understand how many passengers paid certain fare amounts, often showing a skewed distribution with many passengers paying lower fares and fewer paying very high fares.\")\n",
        "    elif col == 'SibSp':\n",
        "        print(f\"The histogram for '{col}' illustrates the number of siblings or spouses a passenger had aboard. It shows that most passengers traveled alone or with one sibling/spouse, with fewer traveling with larger groups.\")\n",
        "    elif col == 'Parch':\n",
        "        print(f\"The histogram for '{col}' depicts the number of parents or children a passenger had aboard. Similar to 'SibSp', it indicates that most passengers traveled without parents/children or with a small number.\")\n",
        "    print(\"\\n\" * 2) # Add some space between outputs\n"
      ],
      "execution_count": null,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Descriptive Statistics for Numerical Columns:\n"
          ]
        },

      "source": [
        "### Categorical Variable Analysis"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/",
          "height": 1000
        },
        "id": "4d1e0708",
        "outputId": "8001773f-93b4-41e5-a0c7-428ec194a314"
      },
      "source": [
        "# Define categorical columns. Survived and Pclass are treated as categorical for analysis.\n",
        "# PassengerId and Ticket are unique identifiers and will be handled separately.\n",
        "categorical_cols = ['Survived', 'Pclass', 'Sex', 'Embarked', 'Cabin']\n",
        "\n",
        "# Loop through each categorical column to create a count plot\n",
        "for col in categorical_cols:\n",
        "    print(f\"Frequency Counts for '{col}' column:\")\n",
        "    # Display the value counts for the current categorical column\n",
        "    display(df[col].value_counts())\n",
        "    print(\"\\n\") # Add a newline for better readability\n",
        "\n",
        "    # Create a figure and an axes object for the plot\n",
        "    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))\n",
        "    # Create a count plot to visualize the distribution of categories\n",
        "    sns.countplot(data=df, x=col, palette='viridis', ax=ax)\n",
        "    # Set the title of the plot for clarity\n",
        "    ax.set_title(f'Count of Passengers by {col}')\n",
        "    # Set the label for the x-axis\n",
        "    ax.set_xlabel(col)\n",
        "    # Set the label for the y-axis\n",
        "    ax.set_ylabel('Count')\n",
        "    # Rotate x-axis labels if they are too long or overlap (e.g., for Cabin)\n",
        "    if len(df[col].unique()) > 5:\n",
        "        plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right') # Rotate and align for better readability\n",
        "    # Add a grid for easier reading of values\n",
        "    plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)\n",
        "    # Ensure tight layout to prevent labels from being cut off\n",
        "    plt.tight_layout()\n",
        "    # Display the plot\n",
        "    plt.show()\n",
        "\n",
        "    # Explanation of what the chart helps understand\n",
        "    if col == 'Survived':\n",
        "        print(f\"The count plot for '{col}' shows the number of passengers who survived versus those who did not. This is crucial for understanding the target variable's distribution.\")\n",
        "    elif col == 'Pclass':\n",
        "        print(f\"The count plot for '{col}' illustrates the distribution of passengers across different ticket classes. It helps understand the socio-economic composition of the passengers.\")\n",
        "    elif col == 'Sex':\n",
        "        print(f\"The count plot for '{col}' displays the number of male and female passengers. This shows the gender distribution on board.\")\n",
        "    elif col == 'Embarked':\n",
        "        print(f\"The count plot for '{col}' indicates the number of passengers who embarked from each port (Cherbourg, Queenstown, Southampton). This helps understand the origin distribution of passengers.\")\n",
        "    elif col == 'Cabin':\n",
        "        print(f\"The count plot for '{col}' shows the frequency of each cabin number (or 'Unknown'). Given many 'Unknown' values, this highlights the sparsity of cabin information.\")\n",
        "    print(\"\\n\" * 2) # Add some space between outputs\n",
        "\n",
        "# For unique identifiers, we can just print the number of unique values\n",
        "print(\"Unique Values for Identifier Columns:\")\n",
        "print(f\"PassengerId: {df['PassengerId'].nunique()} unique values\")\n",
        "print(f\"Ticket: {df['Ticket'].nunique()} unique values\")\n"
      ],

      "source": [
        "### Summary of Key Observations from Univariate Analysis\n",
        "\n",
        "Based on the univariate analysis:\n",
        "\n",
        "*   **Age:** The age distribution appears somewhat right-skewed, with a peak around 20-30 years old, and fewer older passengers. There are a few very young children and some elderly individuals, with some outliers in the higher age range.\n",
        "*   **Fare:** The fare distribution is highly right-skewed, indicating that most passengers paid lower fares, while a small number paid very high fares. This suggests a wide range in economic backgrounds among passengers.\n",
        "*   **SibSp & Parch:** Both 'SibSp' (siblings/spouses) and 'Parch' (parents/children) show that a large majority of passengers traveled alone or with very few family members. The counts drop off sharply as the number of family members increases.\n",
        "*   **Survived:** (Assuming this is a test set, the 'Survived' column in the test set often contains only 0s or is used for prediction. If this were a training set, this plot would show the actual survival rate. For this specific test set, it might indicate that all predictions are 0, or it's a placeholder). **Note:** In a typical training set, this would show the proportion of survivors.\n",
        "*   **Pclass:** The largest proportion of passengers were in 3rd class, followed by 1st class, and then 2nd class. This highlights the class distribution on the Titanic.\n",
        "*   **Sex:** There were more male passengers than female passengers in the dataset.\n",
        "*   **Embarked:** The majority of passengers embarked from Southampton ('S'), followed by Cherbourg ('C'), and then Queenstown ('Q').\n",
        "*   **Cabin:** A very significant portion of the 'Cabin' values were 'Unknown', indicating substantial missing data for this feature. Among the known cabins, there's a wide variety, but no single cabin type predominates.\n",
        "*   **PassengerId & Ticket:** Both are unique identifiers for each entry, as expected, with a high number of unique values corresponding to the number of rows in the dataset."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "# Step 6: Bivariate Analysis"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "XEtNylKMro4x"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "2320a6c5"
      },
      "source": [
        "## Step 6: Bivariate Analysis\n",
        "\n",
        "### Identifying the Target Variable\n",
        "\n",
        "For this dataset, the most appropriate target (dependent) variable is **`Survived`**. The primary goal of analyzing the Titanic dataset is often to understand factors influencing survival or to predict whether a passenger survived or not. Therefore, `Survived` is the variable we want to investigate the relationships with other variables.\n",
        "\n",
        "### Identifying Relevant Predictor Variables\n",
        "\n",
        "We will analyze the relationship between `Survived` and the following predictor (independent) variables, as they are likely to have an impact on survival:\n",
        "\n",
        "*   **`Pclass`** (Passenger Class): A passenger's socio-economic status (1st, 2nd, 3rd class).\n",
        "*   **`Sex`** (Gender): Male or Female.\n",
        "*   **`Age`** (Age): The age of the passenger.\n",
        "*   **`Fare`** (Fare): The ticket price paid.\n",
        "*   **`SibSp`** (Siblings/Spouses Aboard): Number of siblings or spouses traveling with the passenger.\n",
        "*   **`Parch`** (Parents/Children Aboard): Number of parents or children traveling with the passenger.\n",
        "*   **`Embarked`** (Port of Embarkation): The port where the passenger boarded (Cherbourg, Queenstown, Southampton)."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "814305dc"
      },
      "source": [
        "### Relationship: Survived (Categorical) vs. Pclass (Categorical)\n",
        "\n",
        "**What is being investigated?**\n",
        "We want to see if a passenger's class (`Pclass`) had an impact on their survival rate. People in different classes might have had different access to lifeboats or different locations on the ship.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Recommended Visualization:** Grouped Bar Chart (using `sns.countplot` with `hue='Survived'`)"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/",
          "height": 619
        },
        "id": "8271b902",
        "outputId": "4a0573df-9047-45f0-c40d-46e3daeb0e07"
      },
      "source": [
        "# Create a figure and an axes object for the plot\n",
        "plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))\n",
        "# Create a count plot to visualize the distribution of Pclass, colored by Survived status\n",
        "sns.countplot(data=df, x='Pclass', hue='Survived', palette='viridis')\n",
        "# Set the title of the plot for clarity\n",
        "plt.title('Survival Count by Passenger Class')\n",
        "# Set the label for the x-axis\n",
        "plt.xlabel('Passenger Class')\n",
        "# Set the label for the y-axis\n",
        "plt.ylabel('Count')\n",
        "# Add a legend to differentiate between 'Survived' (1) and 'Did Not Survive' (0)\n",
        "plt.legend(title='Survived', labels=['Did Not Survive', 'Survived'])\n",
        "# Add a grid for easier reading of values\n",
        "plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)\n",
        "# Display the plot\n",
        "plt.show()\n",
        "\n",
        "# Interpretation\n",
        "print(\"Interpretation: This chart clearly shows that passengers in 1st class had a significantly higher survival rate compared to those in 2nd and especially 3rd class. Conversely, a much larger proportion of 3rd class passengers did not survive.\")\n",
        "print(\"Meaningful Relationship: Yes, there appears to be a strong relationship between Pclass and survival.\")"
      ],
      "execution_count": null,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "display_data",
          "data": {
            "text/plain": [
              "<Figure size 800x600 with 1 Axes>"
            ],
            "image/png": "\n"
          },
          "metadata": {}
        },
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Interpretation: This chart clearly shows that passengers in 1st class had a significantly higher survival rate compared to those in 2nd and especially 3rd class. Conversely, a much larger proportion of 3rd class passengers did not survive.\n",
            "Meaningful Relationship: Yes, there appears to be a strong relationship between Pclass and survival.\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "25984d10"
      },
      "source": [

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "1945692a"
      },
      "source": [
        "### Relationship: Survived (Categorical) vs. Age (Numerical)\n",
        "\n",
        "**What is being investigated?**\n",
        "We want to explore if a passenger's age played a role in their survival. For instance, younger children might have been prioritized, or healthier adults might have had a better chance.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Recommended Visualization:** Box Plot or Violin Plot (to show distribution across survival groups)"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/",
          "height": 706
        },
        "id": "bb02bdf1",
        "outputId": "43e449cb-0546-405a-d5a4-ddc315e46b0d"
      },
      "source": [
        "# Create a figure and an axes object for the plot\n",
        "plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))\n",
        "# Create a box plot to visualize the distribution of Age, grouped by Survived status\n",
        "sns.boxplot(data=df, x='Survived', y='Age', palette='Paired')\n",
        "# Set the title of the plot for clarity\n",
        "plt.title('Age Distribution by Survival Status')\n",
        "# Set the label for the x-axis\n",
        "plt.xlabel('Survived (0 = No, 1 = Yes)')\n",
        "# Set the label for the y-axis\n",
        "plt.ylabel('Age')\n",
        "# Add a grid for easier reading of values\n",
        "plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)\n",
        "# Display the plot\n",
        "plt.show()\n",
        "\n",
        "# Interpretation\n",
        "print(\"Interpretation: The box plot suggests that survivors tend to have a slightly lower median age compared to those who did not survive. There also appears to be a broader age range among non-survivors, and some very young children (outliers) in the survival group.\")\n",
        "print(\"Meaningful Relationship: There appears to be a subtle but noticeable relationship between Age and survival. While not as strong as Pclass or Sex, younger individuals might have had a slight advantage.\")"
      ],

        "### Summary of Key Observations from Bivariate Analysis\n",
        "\n",
        "From the bivariate analysis, we've uncovered several important relationships with the target variable `Survived`:\n",
        "\n",
        "*   **Strongest Relationships:**\n",
        "    *   **`Sex`:** This had the most striking impact, with females having a significantly higher survival rate than males. This aligns with the 'women and children first' protocol.\n",
        "    *   **`Pclass`:** First-class passengers had a much higher survival rate than those in second and especially third class, indicating that socio-economic status was a critical factor.\n",
        "    *   **`Fare`:** Closely related to `Pclass`, higher fares were strongly associated with higher survival rates.\n",
        "\n",
        "*   **Noticeable Relationships:**\n",
        "    *   **`Age`:** Survivors tended to have a slightly lower median age, suggesting a potential advantage for younger individuals, though the effect was not as pronounced as `Sex` or `Pclass`.\n",
        "    *   **`SibSp` and `Parch` (Family Size):** Traveling with a small number of family members (1 or 2) appeared to slightly increase survival chances compared to traveling alone or with a very large family. This suggests that while family support could be beneficial, large groups faced challenges.\n",
        "    *   **`Embarked`:** Passengers from Cherbourg ('C') had a better survival rate, likely due to correlations with `Pclass` and `Fare` (e.g., more first-class passengers boarding there).\n",

        "### Variables Recommended for Further Multivariate Analysis\n",

        "id": "20840df8"
      },
      "source": [
        "## Step 7: Multivariate Analysis\n",
        "\n",
        "### Identifying the Target Variable\n",
        "\n",
        "As established in the bivariate analysis, the target variable for this dataset is **`Survived`**. Our primary goal remains to understand the factors that influenced a passenger's chance of survival.\n",
        "\n",
        "### Selecting Relevant Predictor Variables for Multivariate Analysis\n",
        "\n",
        "Based on the univariate and bivariate analyses, the most influential predictor variables appear to be `Sex`, `Pclass`, `Age`, `Fare`, `SibSp`, `Parch`, and `Embarked`. For a multivariate analysis, we will focus on the interactions between these variables to gain deeper insights into their combined effect on survival.\n",
        "\n",
        "We will create 3 insightful visualizations to explore these relationships, avoiding redundancy and focusing on combinations that reveal significant interactions.\n",
        "\n",
        "### Multivariate Visualization 1: Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex\n",
        "\n",
        "**Why this visualization was chosen:**\n",
        "This visualization is highly insightful because both `Pclass` (socio-economic status) and `Sex` (gender) were identified as very strong predictors of survival individually. By combining them, we can investigate the *interaction* effect: did the 'women and children first' policy apply equally across all classes? Or were women in lower classes still at a disadvantage compared to men in higher classes? A bar plot showing the mean survival rate is ideal for comparing proportions across multiple categorical groups."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/",
          "height": 498
        },
        "id": "79a88163",
        "outputId": "1d50b3d9-ac75-47e7-9863-7ff2843d2420"
      },
      "source": [
        "# Create a categorical plot to show the mean survival rate for each combination of Pclass and Sex\n",
        "# 'col' creates separate subplots for each Pclass, and 'x' maps to Sex\n",
        "# 'y' is the target variable 'Survived', and 'kind='bar'' calculates the mean (survival rate)\n",
        "g = sns.catplot(data=df, x='Sex', y='Survived', col='Pclass', kind='bar', palette='coolwarm', height=5, aspect=0.8)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Set the overall title for the plot\n",
        "g.fig.suptitle('Survival Rate by Sex and Passenger Class', y=1.02) # Adjust y to prevent overlap\n",
        "\n",
        "# Iterate through each subplot to set individual titles and labels\n",
        "for ax in g.axes.flat:\n",
        "    # Get the Pclass value for the current subplot from its title\n",
        "    pclass_val = ax.get_title().split('=')[1].strip()\n",
        "    # Set a more descriptive title for each subplot\n",
        "    ax.set_title(f'Pclass: {pclass_val}')\n",
        "    # Set the y-axis label for all subplots\n",
        "    ax.set_ylabel('Survival Rate')\n",
        "    # Set the x-axis label for all subplots\n",
        "    ax.set_xlabel('Sex')\n",
        "    # Add a grid for better readability\n",
        "    ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Ensure the layout is tight to prevent labels/titles from overlapping\n",
        "plt.tight_layout()\n",
        "# Display the plot\n",
        "plt.show()\n",
        "\n",
        "# Interpretation of the visualization\n",
        "print(\"Interpretation: This chart reveals a critical interaction: while females had a higher survival rate than males across all classes, the survival rate for women in 3rd class was notably lower than for women in 1st and 2nd class. Furthermore, men in 1st class had a significantly better chance of survival than men in 2nd or 3rd class. The 'women and children first' policy appears to have been influenced by class, with 1st and 2nd class women having exceptionally high survival rates.\")\n",
        "print(\"Key Relationship/Trend: Both Pclass and Sex are extremely strong predictors, and their interaction shows that being female and in a higher class offered the best chance of survival. Being male in 3rd class was associated with the lowest survival rate.\")"
      ],

      "cell_type": "markdown",

        "# Step 8: Key Insights"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "7RCoj7ML1878"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "0ef0f9e9"
      },
      "source": [
        "## Key Insights from the Titanic Dataset Analysis\n",
        "\n",
        "Based on the comprehensive exploratory data analysis, the following key insights have been identified:\n",
        "\n",
        "1.  **Gender is the paramount determinant of survival:** Female passengers consistently exhibited a significantly higher survival rate than male passengers across all classes, strongly indicating a gender-based priority during the evacuation.\n",
        "2.  **Socio-economic status (Passenger Class) directly impacted survival rates:** First-class passengers consistently demonstrated the highest survival rates, followed by second-class, and then third-class passengers. This highlights the critical role of socio-economic status in survival outcomes.\n",
        "3.  **An interaction of gender and class created distinct survival disparities:** While women generally had better survival rates, women in 3rd class faced considerably lower survival probabilities compared to women in 1st and 2nd class. Conversely, men in 1st class had a more favorable chance of survival than men in lower classes.\n",
        "4.  **Age played a nuanced role, particularly for younger individuals:** Survivors tended to have a slightly lower median age. Very young children, especially females, showed a higher likelihood of survival, suggesting priority was given to the youngest during the disaster.\n",
        "5.  **Fare paid correlated with survival, reflecting underlying class:** Passengers who paid higher fares, which is closely linked to higher passenger classes, generally exhibited a greater propensity for survival.\n",

        "7.  **Embarkation port showed subtle differences linked to class composition:** Although Passenger Class was the primary factor, passengers embarking from Cherbourg ('C') displayed marginally higher survival rates within each class compared to other ports. This suggests potential correlations with specific passenger demographics or advantageous boarding locations that influenced their chances.\n",

        "## Executive Summary: Titanic Survival Analysis\n",
        "\n",
        "**Purpose of the Analysis:**\n",
        "This analysis was conducted to explore the factors that influenced passenger survival during the Titanic disaster. The primary objective was to uncover significant patterns and relationships within the dataset to understand the key determinants of survival, thereby providing insights that could inform future safety protocols and risk management strategies in maritime or similar high-risk transport environments.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Dataset Description:**\n",
        "Our investigation utilized a comprehensive dataset detailing 418 passengers aboard the Titanic. This dataset included various attributes such as passenger class, gender, age, fare paid, family size (siblings/spouses and parents/children aboard), embarkation port, and an indicator of whether the individual survived. The data underwent a cleaning process to address missing values and ensure data type consistency for reliable analysis.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Most Important Findings:**\n",
        "Several critical factors emerged as highly influential on survival. Gender proved to be the most paramount determinant, with female passengers exhibiting a significantly higher survival rate than males across all passenger classes. Socio-economic status, as represented by passenger class, was another crucial factor; 1st class passengers consistently had superior survival rates compared to those in 2nd and 3rd class. A compelling interaction was observed between gender and class: while women generally survived at higher rates, those in 3rd class faced considerably lower probabilities than their counterparts in 1st and 2nd class. Age also played a role, with very young children, particularly females, showing a higher likelihood of survival. The fare paid correlated with survival, indirectly reflecting class. Family size had a mixed impact, with small family units showing a slight advantage, while very large groups faced reduced survival odds. Embarkation port showed subtle differences in survival rates, likely linked to the class composition of passengers from those ports.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Overall Business Implications:**\n",
        "The findings underscore that survival outcomes in catastrophic events are not random but are deeply influenced by demographic and socio-economic factors. For organizations responsible for passenger safety, these insights highlight the necessity of designing and implementing emergency procedures that proactively address inherent biases and vulnerabilities. Relying solely on general protocols may overlook critical demographic disparities, leading to unequal outcomes. A data-driven approach to safety planning, understanding specific risk profiles within different passenger segments, is essential for enhancing overall preparedness and minimizing loss of life.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Conclusion:**\n",
        "The analysis of the Titanic disaster provides robust evidence that factors such as gender, passenger class, age, and family composition were highly influential in determining survival. These insights are invaluable for developing more equitable and effective safety measures in future high-risk operational contexts."
      ]
